pwd prints the folder you are in. Task: show your current folder.
mkdir creates a folder. Task: create a folder called notes.
echo prints text and > writes it into a file. Task: write any text into notes/a.txt.
cat shows what is inside a file. Task: show notes/a.txt.
cp copies a file. Task: copy notes/a.txt to notes/b.txt.
ls lists files; ls -l adds details. Task: list the notes folder.
wc -l counts lines. Task: count the lines of notes/a.txt.
A pipe | sends one command's output into another. Task: count the files in notes with ls and wc -l.
>> adds to the end of a file instead of replacing it. Task: add a second line to notes/a.txt.
Variables keep values: NAME=Ali; then $NAME uses it. Task: set a variable and echo it on one line (use ;).
grep finds lines that contain a word. Task: search for a word inside notes/a.txt.
A script is a file of commands; chmod +x makes it runnable. Task: echo 'echo hi' > hi.sh && chmod +x hi.sh
git tracks the history of a project. Task: create a repository: git init proj
Every project needs a README. Task: write a line into proj/README.md (echo … > proj/README.md).
git add puts a change on the stage. Task: git -C proj add README.md
git commit saves the staged change in history. Task: git -C proj commit -m "first commit"
git log shows the history. Task: show the log of proj (git -C proj log --oneline).
python3 -c runs a line of Python. Task: print the result of 2+3 with python3 -c.
Python programs live in .py files. Task: create hello.py that prints a greeting (echo 'print("Hi")' > hello.py).
Run a program with python3 file.py. Task: run hello.py.
for … in range(n) repeats. Task: print 0, 1, 2 with a for loop in python3 -c.
curl talks to web servers; -I shows only the headers. Task: curl -I https://example.com
-o saves the page to a file. Task: save https://example.com as page.html with curl.
Every page has a <title>. Task: find it with grep title page.html
